featured_reviews.name: Ilina Banerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tandel's Kitchen in Mahim Seafood Plaza is an extraordinary culinary gem where the ladies of the Koli community masterfully prepare some of the best seafood I've ever tasted. Nestled along the scenic Mahim Sea Beach, with a breathtaking view of the Bandra-Worli Sealink and the soothing Arabian Sea breeze, this place offers more than just food—it's an experience.

During my visit, I had the pleasure of trying several dishes, each leaving a lasting impression. The Surmai Fry was nothing short of spectacular. The fish was incredibly fresh, a testament to their daily fishing activities, and it was cooked to perfection with a flavorful blend of spices that brought out the best in the surmai.

The Prawn Fry was another highlight. The prawns had a perfectly crispy outer layer that gave way to tender, juicy insides. The balance of textures and the well-seasoned coating made each bite a delight.

One of the most memorable dishes was the Clams Masala Curry. It was delightfully spicy, striking a perfect balance that kept it exciting without being overwhelming. The curry had a chatpata (tangy and spicy) taste that was utterly addictive. Paired with the extremely soft Bhakri (a type of flatbread), it created a harmonious combination that was both comforting and satisfying.

What sets Tandel's Kitchen apart is not only the freshness of their seafood but also the unique spice mixes they create in-house. These spices, prepared in a homely style, infuse the dishes with flavors that are rich, vibrant, and authentically Koli.

The ambiance of Tandel's Kitchen significantly enhances the dining experience. Enjoying such flavorful seafood while overlooking the serene Arabian Sea and the iconic Bandra-Worli Sealink, all with the cool sea breeze enveloping you, creates a dining atmosphere that is both relaxing and invigorating.

Tandel's Kitchen is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic and extraordinary seafood experience in Mumbai. The combination of fresh, expertly cooked seafood, unique and flavorful spices, and a perfect seaside setting makes it a standout destination. Whether you are a local or a visitor, this place promises a meal that you will not forget.

featured_reviews.name: Hrishikesh Chinchalikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌴 A Heartwarming Goan Experience at a Portuguese Restaurant 🌴

Dining at this Goan Portuguese restaurant was truly a delightful experience. From the first bite to the last note of live music, everything felt authentic, soulful, and unforgettable.

The food was absolutely amazing—rich in flavor, perfectly balanced, and deeply rooted in Goan tradition. Every dish reflected care, passion, and mastery of recipes passed down through generations.

⭐ Special Dishes We Tried:

Coconut Cashew Bhaji – A standout vegetarian dish, creamy, mildly spiced, and incredibly comforting. The coconut and cashew combination was simply delicious.

Surmai Fish Kalvam – A must-try for fish lovers. Fresh surmai cooked in a flavorful Goan-style curry that was bold, aromatic, and unforgettable.

Live Music by Uncle – The soulful live music added magic to the evening, creating a warm and joyful Goan vibe that elevated the entire dining experience.

What truly made this place special was the personal touch. The owner personally visited every table, warmly sharing the inspiring journey of how the restaurant began. He spoke about his wife’s culinary journey and her exceptional talent as a cook—the heart behind the delicious recipes served here. Listening to their story made the food taste even better, knowing it comes from passion, dedication, and love.

The restaurant has grown into multiple branches, including international locations, and it’s easy to see why. This place is not just about food—it’s about culture, stories, and genuine hospitality.

✨ Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Goan cuisine, soulful music, and heartfelt hospitality. A place you’ll want to visit again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Leena Surve
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goa Portuguese is a must stop in my every visit to Mumbai (from USA). This place has such a fun vibe with awesome food. There Goan and malvani dishes remind me of my mom’s home cooking.   We always start with Bombay duck fry and shrimp koliwada. Then the order including tisarya sukhe, chicken xacuti, pomfret / surmai dishes, amboli, vade continues so much that we get warned by the waiter ‘jara jast hoil ho’ (might be little to much). But we love their food so much that the warning, even though correct, gets ignored.
Even after visiting so many times, we have managed to touch very less amounts of dishes offered. Must increase our visits.
This time was lucky to meet with Dr. Suhas Awchat (co-founder). A warm personality and all the praise for master chef, Mrs. Deepa Awchat (he openly gave the credit of starting and owning the restaurant completely  to her, indicating that after army, she is his boss 😀).

A Seafood Disaster – Masooli Restaurant

Visited Masooli expecting good seafood. What we got was very disappointing.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: sonia mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s been a while since we’ve enjoyed an authentic Maharashtrian meal! At first glance the place makes your feel right at home, very true to its name! We had such a great meal on Sunday, we were three of us - my brother, my sister and I.
The best thing to do when you visit is let the owner suggest their specials for you to eat, we didn’t even open the menu - we tried the Chonak Fry - 10/10, we tried the Bombil fry- 12/10 ( the filling inside the Bombil blew our mind, we had the Alu Wadi with Prawns filling - 10/10!
For main course we had the Amti with Rice Bhakri and Ravas Fry ( the Ravas so incredibly fresh) the main course was 10/10 and to top it off we also tried their Prawns Bhaat / Pulav - it was so damn good! 100/10….the Sol Kadis we tasted took us back home honestly. After this meal all we needed was our bed to sleep on cause we were in a complete food coma. An absolutely outstanding meal with a very comfortable seating and ambiance! A definite must visit again and again!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

featured_reviews.name: KPExplorer
featured_reviews.review_text: This resturant in primiraly from Pune which is only one in Mumbai Dadar kohinoor is was way beyond expectations .. good try for fish lovers, with great service from staff to decently priced thalis. They start with timbal a kokum drink as apetiser. Their fish curry is very delicious with perfect taste. They also serve senior citizen thali at 450 in which they gave 2 fish fry. Crab thali was also great. Their Ghavna with curry is an amazing combination

featured_reviews.name: guptepooja
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place and way better than the Pune branch. It's open from 11.30am to 11pm...so you get served even at 5pm

They cook fresh stuff so order may take time but it's fresh! Amazing taste and super fresh fish. Blessed to have this joint in Dadar which works as a perfect combination of fresh seafood+ authentic goan cuisine+ economical.  We ordered mutton + pomfret fry thali and chicken thali. Fish was super duper fresh. My 6yrs old child finished the meals with no left over food in her plate; which itself is a big compliment.

Soham manages this really well. He also gifted a small soft toy fish to my child for new years.

Let the photos do the justice.

featured_reviews.name: Floyd Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Been on the lookout for good fish thalis in and around dadar

FCR is a very nice place to have one

Reasonable price, well prepared and the quantity served is also not bad

Wide range of thalis from mini to special to varying types

Spacious seating and quick service too

featured_reviews.name: Sunit Katkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saw a lot of food vloggers show this place. Big mistake of believing them. Only good thing is the welcome drink called Tival. The prawns sukka was more curry and rubber like prawns. Only slightly better dish was crab masala. Sol kadhi had no kick. Maybe Gajalee and Sindhudurg have spoilt me by giving very good Sol Kadhi. We asked for Rice Bhakri expecting it to be soft like other places. This felt like it was cooked a day before and just reheated and served. It was too hard to be called a rice Bhakri.

Regret not going to Dutta Boarding House in Parel or even Gomantak next door. Had crab masala last week at Dutta Boarding.. FCR does not have that zing but it's better than the rubber prawn sukka taste.

Sorry, will not believe food vloggers from now on.

featured_reviews.name: Harshad Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Small and cozy. Delicious food. Service is excellent. Prawns Aluwadi is a must try dish.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Bhogade

But as a veg eater, I honestly didn’t enjoy the veg thali at all. If you’re vegetarian, don’t go in with high expectations. For non-veg folks, it’s absolutely worth it.”

featured_reviews.review_text:
A delightful meal at Flavors of Malvan in Prabhadevi! The food is exceptionally tasty, wholesome, and prepared in a way that feels truly home-style, yet packed with authentic coastal flavors.

The Green Chutney Surmai was outstanding, the Fish Curry with rice was comforting and flavorful, and the Koliwada Prawns were perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. To top it all, the Kokum Soda was simply mind-blowing—refreshing, tangy, and the perfect accompaniment to the meal.

A special mention to Vinod and Navin, who were incredibly warm, welcoming, and attentive. They took the time to understand our preferences and suggested dishes that suited our tastes perfectly, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you're looking for authentic Malvani cuisine that combines traditional flavors with heartfelt hospitality, this place is a must-visit!The restaurant is Flavors of Malvan.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

featured_reviews.name: Anvi Kaale
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently had lunch at this restaurant and it was truly a fantastic experience! Authentic malvani taste.😋 The flavors were absolutely amazing, and every dish was prepared to perfection. 💯 I highly recommend trying their delicious offerings. Will definitely be back for more! ✨👍

featured_reviews.name: Preeti Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience of the restaurant was lovely and cozy. We tried the Bombil Tawa Fry, but it was quite oily. We also ordered the Surmai Thali and Pomfret Thali. Everything in the thali was good except for the fish curry, which unfortunately lacked flavor. Solkadi was fresh and awesome in taste.

For desserts, we tried Modak and Puranpoli. The Modak tasted good, although the outer covering was a bit thick.The Puranpoli, however, was absolutely awesome and definitely a highlight.

Overall, it’s a nice and cozy restaurant, especially for non-vegetarian lovers. 🐟🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Guddeti
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful experience at Flavours of Malvan! The Prawns pulav and Bombil Thali were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic Malvani flavors. Fresh seafood, flavorful curries, crispy fry, and refreshing solkadhi made the meal truly satisfying. Highly recommended for seafood lovers looking for an authentic taste of the coast. 🐟🦐😋

featured_reviews.name: Greeshma Gowda
featured_reviews.review_text: Walked into this restaurant when we were in Dadar on a Sunday evening. Its a small restaurant on the ground floor of a residential buidling. There was a waiting time of 30 mins to get in. We ordered the pomfret thalli and crab thalli. The service is slow but it was worth the wait. The crab was soft and well cooked and the gravy was delicious. We also had sweet lime soda and lemon ginger drink. Last we had ukdiche modak which was also tasty.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything tasted like it was cooked in someone’s very talented Malvani aaji’s kitchen. The bombil fry? Illegal levels of good. The mutton sukka + the prawn thali? Had me contemplating licking the plate. The puran poli and the modaks? Felt like a hug in dessert form. Just solid recommendations from the team and great vibes all around.
If you like your food flavourful, fiery, and with zero nonsense, this place is a no-brainer. Will 100% be back.

featured_reviews.name: Jimeet Pawaskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found my new favorite Sunday spot! Being a Malvani…this place is lovely, understated home-style charm that makes you want to settle in and stay a while.
Even with a 45-minute wait on a Sunday, the staff remained gracious and efficient. The Mutton Special Thali is a must-try—rich, authentic, and perfectly executed. It felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like a high-end home-cooked feast!
Full marks overall !

Manager), you can have a wonderful time and excellent food, for sure! And if you are going on Sundays Live Band is complimentary. Make sure to reserve a table. Enjoyment is unlimited! The service is top of the line and food is also very delicious & Tempting. The overall Atmosphere and Ambience is also very Superb, Fantabulous, Amazing & Excellent. Worth coming here again.

featured_reviews.name: Paurnima Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Coast & Bloom at Dadar and it turned out to be a truly memorable dining experience that beautifully celebrates coastal and regional Indian flavors with a refined touch.

We began with the Lobster Thermidor, which was served in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce accompanied by sautéed vegetables, bread, and a perfectly cooked egg. The dish was indulgent, flavorful, and luxuriously satisfying. Alongside, we had the Tandoori Prawns, which carried an excellent smoky char from the tandoor. Paired with fresh green chutney and a sweet-tangy mango pickle, the combination elevated the entire starter experience.

For the main course, we opted for the Malvani Fish Curry with Ravas. The fish was exceptionally fresh, tender, and cooked to perfection, soaking beautifully in the aromatic Malvani gravy. We also tried the Chettinad Chicken, which had a bold, spicy profile and was packed with deep, authentic flavors.

To complement the curries, we had Malabar Parotta, Ghavane, and Chilli Cheese Garlic Naan. Each bread brought a different texture and paired wonderfully with the gravies, with the ghavane being a particularly delightful and unique accompaniment.

We also enjoyed Solkadi, which perfectly balanced the meal with its refreshing, lightly spiced tanginess. For drinks, we tried the Ratamba (kokum-based), Navy Punch, and Ginger Ale, all of which were refreshing and well-crafted.

To end the meal, we had the Crab Meat Fried Rice. While pleasant, this was comparatively simpler in flavor and had lesser crab meat than expected.

What truly stood out, beyond the food, was the exceptional service. The staff member assisting us went above and beyond — offering curry samples when we were confused between options and even showing us the raw fish to help us understand the portion and quality we would be served. Such thoughtful hospitality added immense value to the experience.

The entire meal came to ₹8,236, and considering the quality of ingredients, variety of dishes, and outstanding service, it felt well worth the price.

Coast & Bloom is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates coastal cuisine served with elegance, authenticity, and warm hospitality.

The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Ferry Wharf few days ago on a weekday. I found it not too busy, very comfortable and aesthetics are great as well of the restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text: This spot offers an uncomplicated dining experience. Short steel stools are arranged alongside taller plastic ones, allowing you to choose from a selection of five daily thalis. The dining hours are from 11.30am to 3.30pm, but remember that it's a cramped living room in a small home, where the kitchen staff, predominantly ladies, serve up fresh seafood. The simplicity of their limited menu adds to the appeal, presented on an unassuming Marathi chalkboard. Those who ordered the chicken thali were given a second serving of chicken gravy. Opting for the pomfret thali, I enjoyed the crispy bombils (the highlight) and mostly overcooked prawns, resulting in a mostly decent meal. featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Fresh Catch on 4 June 2026 and it was excellent!  I asked the bartender to create me a great custom drink and he exceeded my expectations with refreshing and unique creations. My waiter, Lawrence, was extremely helpful in bombil suggestions as well as sourcing from off menu fish. Try Fresh Catch you won’t be disappointed with the drinks, food or service. Ask for Lawrence!

featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh Catch by Francis is located on the 2nd Floor. Lift available. Had the Prawn pulao and Surmai Rossa Curry with Bombil rava fry. Delicious food and good quality for 2 people

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had heard a lot about Gomantak in Dadar. On my recent visit, I finally decided to try it. It was raining heavily that day. Even then, the restaurant was completely packed. They have both AC and non-AC sections. I had to wait for about 15 to 20 minutes before getting a table. The crowd itself gave me a sense of how popular this place is among seafood lovers.

I ordered the Chicken Masala Thali and Crab Masala with Rice Bhakri. The Chicken Masala Thali came with Chicken Gravy, Chicken Rassa, Rice, Bhakri, Sol Kadi, and Salad. The Chicken Gravy had a rich flavour that reminded me of coastal Goan cooking. It had depth, warmth, and a balance of spice. The Chicken Rassa was light and paired beautifully with rice. The Sol Kadi worked as a refreshing sip after the gravies.

The Crab Masala was the highlight of the meal. The crab meat was fresh and sweet. The masala was layered with flavour and had the right amount of spice. The meat absorbed the masala so well that every bite felt satisfying. The staff even help you break the crab if needed, which makes it easier to enjoy. The Rice Bhakri was soft and thick. It soaked up the masala and gravies perfectly.

To finish, I ordered the Caramel Custard. It was smooth, light, and mildly sweet. It balanced the spice of the seafood dishes.

Gomantak is a family-style restaurant that focuses on good food rather than frills. The service was courteous and attentive. The prices are fair for the portions and quality. It is a reliable place in Dadar if you are looking for seafood that feels authentic and comforting.

Ratings:
Quality – 4/5
Quantity – 4.1/5
Service – 4/5
Price – ₹800 for 2 people

For more food experiences, follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!
